questions.q: Which treatment plan applies to me?
questions.a: Day 1: folinic acid and fluorouracil injection, followed by a 46-hour fluorouracil pump. Repeat every 14 days. Adjuvant treatment: up to 12 cycles; advanced treatment: continue only while appropriate. Your team confirms any modification.

questions.q: Do more side effects mean treatment is working?
questions.a: No. Side effects do not reliably measure response. Report symptoms and follow the agreed review plan.

title: Fluorouracil + folinic acid every 14 days
review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending
indication_text: Adjuvant or advanced colorectal adenocarcinoma; every 14 days.
purpose: Treatment after colorectal cancer surgery can reduce recurrence risk. For advanced cancer, treatment aims to control the disease. Your team confirms which aim applies.
schedule_summary: Day 1: folinic acid and fluorouracil injection, followed by a 46-hour fluorouracil pump. Repeat every 14 days. Adjuvant treatment: up to 12 cycles; advanced treatment: continue only while appropriate.
administration_text: Folinic acid 400 mg/m² IV over 30 minutes, then fluorouracil 400 mg/m² IV bolus and 2400 mg/m² over 46 hours. Folinic acid is held/omitted with bolus fluorouracil.

agents.name: Folinic acid
agents.explanation: Folinic acid helps fluorouracil remain bound to an enzyme needed to make DNA. In this regimen it increases fluorouracil activity and can also increase its unwanted effects. It is not a vitamin supplement to start yourself.
agents.watch: The combined treatment can increase mouth soreness and diarrhoea. Report these promptly. Rare allergic reactions can occur.

agents.name: Fluorouracil
agents.explanation: Fluorouracil interferes with DNA and RNA, the instructions cells need to grow. The same drug has different schedules; follow the prescription for this regimen.
agents.watch: Report diarrhoea, mouth sores, painful hands or feet and unexpected severe early symptoms. Chest pain needs urgent assessment even after a normal DPD test.
risks: Severe early toxicity including DPD-related toxicity

day_groups.body: Confirm the 46-hour finish time and disconnection appointment. Side effects can occur on any day; the calendar does not predict when you will feel well.
day_groups.action: Call the oncology team if unwell. Do not change pump settings or disconnect it yourself unless specifically trained and instructed.

support.title: Supportive medicines
support.text: Use the prescribed anti-sickness and diarrhoea plan; check the medicine, timing and rescue duration. Do not duplicate steroids or anti-sickness medicines.

support.title: Mouth, bowel and skin care
support.text: Report soreness and diarrhoea early. Use gentle mouth and skin care and ask for help with food or fluids.

support.title: Medicine checks
support.text: Bring all prescription medicines, supplements and non-prescription products. Warfarin and phenytoin may need closer monitoring; brivudine/sorivudine interactions require pharmacy review.

support.title: Pump and line support
support.text: Confirm the pump-care instructions and a working contact number. Do not adjust, reconnect or disconnect the pump unless specifically trained and instructed.

sections.title: Before treatment
sections.text: Confirm the treatment aim, duration, DPD result, blood tests, prescription and contact numbers.

sections.title: Visits and access
sections.text: Day 1: folinic acid and fluorouracil injection, followed by a 46-hour fluorouracil pump. Repeat every 14 days. Adjuvant treatment: up to 12 cycles; advanced treatment: continue only while appropriate. Confirm line access, pump changes and disconnection arrangements.

sections.title: If treatment is delayed
sections.text: Ask for revised written treatment and support-medicine instructions. Do not make up missed doses or carry an old plan into a new phase.

sections.title: Getting help
sections.text: Keep the wallet card and medicine list available. Contact the team promptly for infection, dehydration, chest symptoms or significant toxicity.

urgent_extra: Contact oncology immediately for fever, shivering, sudden illness, severe diarrhoea, inability to drink, very little urine or unusual bleeding. New severe chest pain, collapse or major breathing difficulty needs emergency help.
consent_support: Confirm treatment aim, expected benefit, reasonable alternatives and no-treatment/supportive-care options. Discuss DPD, infection, mouth/bowel/skin toxicity, cardiac symptoms, fertility, contraception, breastfeeding and interactions. Explain line/pump risks and response to malfunction.

items.title: Why this treatment?
items.text: Treatment after colorectal cancer surgery can reduce recurrence risk. For advanced cancer, treatment aims to control the disease. Your team confirms which aim applies.

items.title: Your course
items.text: Day 1: folinic acid and fluorouracil injection, followed by a 46-hour fluorouracil pump. Repeat every 14 days. Adjuvant treatment: up to 12 cycles; advanced treatment: continue only while appropriate.

items.title: Choices
items.text: Discuss the expected benefit, burdens, alternatives and how treatment fits your priorities. You can ask for more time or another explanation before deciding.

items.title: DPD before fluorouracil
items.text: Low DPD activity can cause severe toxicity. Testing helps guide the plan but cannot prevent every reaction. Unexpected severe early symptoms need urgent advice.

items.title: Blood tests
items.text: Before each 14-day cycle: blood count, renal and liver profile; baseline DPD. Scans/markers follow the consultant plan.

items.title: Medicines and interactions
items.text: Bring all prescription medicines, supplements and non-prescription products. Warfarin and phenytoin may need closer monitoring; brivudine/sorivudine interactions require pharmacy review.

items.title: Mouth / eating
items.text: Report painful ulcers or difficulty eating and drinking.

items.title: Chest / heart
items.text: New chest pain needs urgent assessment, including during an infusion.

items.title: Bowel / hydration
items.text: Report diarrhoea, increased stoma output, severe pain, blood or dehydration.

items.title: Hands / feet
items.text: Report painful redness, cracking or peeling that affects daily activity.

items.title: Blood / infection
items.text: Fever, shivers or sudden illness need immediate oncology advice.

items.title: Pump / line
items.text: Report leakage, line pain, swelling, disconnection or a stopped pump immediately.

items.title: Food and fluids
items.text: Aim for tolerable meals and fluids. Report weight loss or poor intake; ask for dietetic support.

items.title: Activity and rest
items.text: Adjust activity and rest to your energy. Report fatigue that limits normal tasks.

items.title: Fertility and sexual health
items.text: Ask about fertility preservation before treatment and the contraception and breastfeeding plan for all medicines. Report a possible pregnancy promptly.

items.title: Support for you and your family
items.text: Ask about counselling, psycho-oncology, practical support, transport and financial advice. Bring someone to discussions if helpful.

items.title: Before leaving
items.text: Check the exact finish or change time, disconnection appointment, line care and 24-hour contact route.

items.title: If something goes wrong
items.text: Report leakage, swelling, line pain, disconnection, an alarm or unexpected pump speed. Follow the supplied spill instructions; do not handle leaked medicine with bare hands.

items.title: Changes to treatment
items.text: Do not restart, reconnect or change the pump unless specifically trained and instructed. The team updates the prescription and pump plan.

evidence.title: Understanding the evidence
evidence.intro: Ask which evidence matches your treatment aim.
evidence.interpretation: The NCCP regimen cites fluorouracil/folinic acid experience in colorectal cancer. Benefits differ by setting; no numerical survival estimate from another schedule is assigned to this exact 14-day regimen.
